''[[On Physical Lines of Force]] → Equations''

Maxwell numbers his equations continuously across all four Parts. This index lists every number that could be '''established''' for this edition, with what it expresses and where it is discussed.

<blockquote>
'''Read this first.''' No equation in the paper could be transcribed from a page scan for this edition. The equation ''numbers'' below are attested — Maxwell cites them by number in running prose, and those references survived transcription. The equation ''bodies'' printed on this wiki are reconstructions in his notation. See [[On Physical Lines of Force/Sources and editorial method|Sources and editorial method]] for the full account and for what would be needed to fix it.
</blockquote>

The eight numbers in bold are the ones a reader is most likely to want.

== Established gaps ==

* '''Part I before (9) and after (19).''' The numbering is not established. Part I appears to run from (1) to about (26), but that is inference from where formulae sit in the prose.
* '''Part II between (58) and (77).''' Unresolved; contradictory readings were obtained.
* '''Part III before (101).''' Where Part III's own numbering begins is unknown.
* '''[[On Physical Lines of Force/Part III/Prop. XVI|Prop. XVI]] carries no printed equation numbers at all.''' This is firmly established, and it is a striking fact: the velocity-of-light calculation, the most famous passage in the paper, is set in unnumbered display.
* '''Part IV.''' No numbered equation could be recovered, and the final equation number of the paper is unknown. Whether Part IV contains numbered Propositions is also unestablished; proposition numbering certainly reaches XVII at the end of [[On Physical Lines of Force/Part III/Prop. XVII|Part III]].
